memory_update.text: Hammond Power Solutions should be tracked as one of the cleanest public-market dry-type transformer and power-quality exposures, but U.S. accessibility and liquidity should be verified because the primary listing is TSX:HPS.A and U.S. trading appears OTC as HMDPF.

Powell Industries is a direct U.S.-listed electrical distribution, medium-voltage switchgear, power-control-room and e-house supplier; include it despite market cap slightly above preferred hunting range because node relevance is unusually direct.

Preformed Line Products is not a transformer name but is a niche second-order T&D hardware supplier that may benefit when grid construction and interconnection work accelerate; keep as underfollowed adjacent candidate requiring stronger node-link verification.

For this node, the highest-quality evidence to collect next is backlog growth, lead-time commentary, capacity additions, customer approvals, data-center and utility order mix, and whether revenue is tied to custom engineered power equipment rather than generic construction exposure.

Need a separate pass for micro-cap speculative exceptions such as Pioneer Power Solutions and for non-U.S. pure plays in Canada, India and Europe; this pass prioritized U.S.-listed or U.S.-accessible names and capped the list at four candidates.

HMDPF should be tracked as the cleanest public pure-play candidate for dry-type transformers and power-quality equipment, but its OTC U.S. listing and Canadian primary listing may complicate liquidity and U.S.-only mandate eligibility.

POWL is a strong switchgear-adjacent candidate with recent data-center evidence, but its market cap now sits around the edge of the preferred underfollowed range and the key risk is lumpy mega-project concentration.
PLPC is an underfollowed second-order grid hardware supplier; include in future passes only if transmission/distribution hardware demand can be tied to concrete utility T&D capex and order growth.

The node should be split in later layers into: direct transformer/power-quality suppliers, medium-voltage switchgear and packaged electrical systems, transmission/distribution line hardware, and diversified reference leaders.

Need a dedicated search for additional U.S.-listed small/mid-cap suppliers in capacitor banks, reactors, harmonic filters, busway, electrical enclosures, relays, breakers, and testing/inspection services tied to data-center and utility power equipment.

HMDPF/HPS.A should be prioritized for Layer 2 verification as the cleanest direct dry-type transformer and power-quality exposure found in this node; key checks are backlog quality, data-center mix, North American capacity, and margin durability.

POWL is a switchgear-adjacent custom electrical distribution candidate with real backlog and product fit, but its market cap is now around $10B+ and attention has increased; verify end-market mix before treating it as underfollowed.

PLPC is not a transformer/power-quality company, but may belong in the broader grid-hardware second-order lane because transmission and distribution hardware can become procurement-critical as utilities expand capacity for data-center and industrial loads.

IESC may capture the installation/integration side of the electrical bottleneck rather than OEM equipment economics; include only if later evidence shows its custom-engineered solutions have power-distribution content and durable margins.

Need a separate pass for true U.S.-listed small-cap transformer/component names, including OTC ADRs, enclosure suppliers, copper/magnet-wire suppliers, testing/certification labs, and electrical distributors that may have less obvious customer dependencies.
HMDPF/HPS.A should be treated as the cleanest direct underfollowed transformer and power-quality candidate for this node, but U.S. accessibility is OTC rather than primary exchange listing.

POWL is a switchgear-adjacent custom power-distribution candidate with data-center and electric-utility relevance, but thesis quality depends on durable mix shift versus lumpy industrial mega-projects.

BELFB is a speculative second-order magnetics/power-conversion candidate; keep only if later evidence links growth to data-center power, UPS, industrial electrification, switchgear, transformer, or grid-equipment OEM customers.

For this node, the best underfollowed angles are not only transformer OEMs but also custom engineered electrical distribution systems, magnetics/power conversion components, and utility/electrical hardware that must be qualified before facilities can be energized.

Need a later pass for non-U.S.-primary but investable global names: Hammond main listing, Indian power-quality/HV equipment suppliers, European transformer and power-quality vendors, and OTC ADRs/foreign ordinaries.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct-public-company universe for the transformer, power-quality, switchgear-adjacent and low/medium-voltage power-distribution node. The cleanest underfollowed exposure found is Hammond Power Solutions via dry-type transformers and power-quality products, though its primary listing is Canadian and the U.S. ticker appears to be OTC. Powell Industries is a direct U.S.-listed custom electrical distribution and switchgear platform with higher attention and a market cap slightly above the preferred hunting range. Preformed Line Products is not a transformer company but is a niche, U.S.-listed second-order grid-hardware beneficiary tied to transmission and distribution buildout. Hubbell is included as a larger reference anchor because its Utility Solutions segment is directly exposed to T&D, substation, distribution, and grid infrastructure demand. Layer 1B expands the stock universe around transformer, power-quality, and switchgear-adjacent bottlenecks. The underfollowed lane is strongest in Hammond Power Solutions, Powell Industries, and Preformed Line Products: each sits one or two steps away from the obvious AI/data-center power story but may benefit if transformer, switchgear, transmission-hardware, and grid-equipment procurement remain schedule-critical. Hubbell is included as a higher-attention reference anchor because it validates the same utility, substation, distribution, and datacenter electrical-equipment demand pool, though it is less pure. Expanded the U.S.-listed/OTC universe for the transformer, power-quality, switchgear-adjacent and low/medium-volt
